blurb:
Somewhere out there is a household that's been missing a 73-pound golden retriever mix and just doesn't know it yet. Leo is four years old, housetrained, good with other dogs, and ready to go. No drama, no project — just a big warm retriever who's already done the hard parts.

High energy, but the good kind. He's going to want to go on walks, play in the yard, and probably take up more than his fair share of the couch. If your household has another dog already, that works fine. Leo gets along.

He's fully vaccinated, heartworm negative, microchipped, and neutered. Walk-ins are welcome at Lewisville Animal Services during visiting hours. The shelter is on College Pkwy in Lewisville.

blurb:
He came in as a stray, a little tucked into himself. That's the description the shelter uses for Hustler, and it's honest. He's a three-and-a-half-year-old pit bull mix who took some time to trust the people around him. He still does. But the staff figured out pretty quickly that calm energy and a treat will get you a long way with this dog.

He's not looking for a loud, chaotic house. He'd do best somewhere patient, where someone's willing to meet him at his pace. That's not a warning — it's just who he is. Dogs like this tend to bond hard once they decide you're their person.

Hustler is fully vaccinated, heartworm negative, microchipped, and neutered. He's listed as uninterested in other dogs, so a one-pet household is probably the right fit. Stop by Lewisville Animal Services on College Pkwy during visiting hours to meet him.

blurb:
Chesney is a three-year-old German Shepherd mix, 68 pounds, high energy, and looking for someone who won't pass her over for one line in her profile. She tested positive for heartworms. That's the thing. And yes, it sounds scary, but here's the reality: heartworm disease is treatable, and Lewisville Animal Services covers her full treatment as part of the adoption. You don't pay for it. You just have to be willing to see it through with her.

She's already vaccinated, microchipped, spayed, and up to date on everything else. The shelter doesn't have detailed notes on her personality yet, but she's a young shepherd mix with high drive — which usually means she's smart, wants a job, and will reward the right owner with serious loyalty.

If you want to know more about exactly how the heartworm treatment works and what to expect, call the shelter directly before you visit. They'll walk you through it. Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville.
shelter_hours: Please call the shelter to confirm visiting hours

• Zero-cost heartworm treatment covered by the shelter is a genuinely newsworthy hook that dismantles the single biggest barrier to her adoption
• A lower source URL ID relative to the other candidates strongly suggests she has been at the shelter the longest, making her the most urgent feature candidate
• Underdog shepherd mix who needs only one willing reader to change her outcome — exactly the high-impact, emotionally resonant story a newsletter exists to tell

blurb:
She's one year old, about 35 pounds, and her whole job in life is to be next to you. That's not an exaggeration. Monica is a hound mix who came into Mostly Mutts from animal control, and the volunteers have been taking great care of her while she waits for the right family to show up.

She's friendly, gentle, and genuinely happy when she's around people. She gets along well with other dogs and would actually do better in a home that already has one. Having a buddy around helps her settle when things get quiet.

Here's what she needs: she has separation anxiety, so a stay-at-home or work-from-home household is the right fit. She also has heartworm and will be starting treatment soon, which means she needs to stay calmer than usual for a stretch while she heals. Local adoption only during treatment. She's currently going through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so call ahead to find out when she's available to meet. Kids 15 and up are the better match given her playful energy around little ones.

She's the kind of dog that will follow you from room to room and think that's the best day she's ever had. If you work from home and want a loyal companion underfoot, call Mostly Mutts at 770-272-6888 to find out when Monica is ready to meet.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Heartworm treatment plus separation anxiety create a compelling underdog narrative that emotionally motivates the right reader
• Prison Pups training program adds institutional credibility and a unique angle that differentiates her from typical shelter dogs
• Medical treatment timeline, local-only restriction, and specialized household needs have extended her wait — urgency is genuine

blurb:
Victor is the dog who wags with his whole body. Not just the tail. His entire back half gets involved when he's excited to see you, which is basically always. He's a five-year-old bulldog mix, about 50 pounds, rescued from animal control by Mostly Mutts, and right now he's living in a foster home where his person leaves the TV on for him when he heads out. Victor seems to enjoy that.

He went through the Prison Pups training program and has the manners to show for it. He's calm at bath time, charmed every volunteer who spent time with him, and his foster calls him a super sweet boy. He can get mouthy when he's wound up, never mean, just excited. That's something to know going in, especially with kids. Teens 15 and up are the better match for him.

He's also working through some leg issues right now, so his foster is helping him rest and recover while he waits for the right home. He'd do best as your only dog. No other dogs, and cats are unknown.

If you want a big personality in a medium-sized package who is going to be genuinely thrilled to see you every single time, Victor is worth a visit. Mostly Mutts is on Chastain Road in Kennesaw. Check their site or give them a call to meet him.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Whole-body wagger with a TV habit and Prison Pups training is an irresistibly visual story that practically writes its own headline
• Active leg recovery adds emotional depth and positions the right adopter as a compassionate hero — strong reader connection hook
• Ongoing medical issue combined with a narrow household profile suggests he has been waiting longer than the average shelter dog

blurb:
She's got floppy ears, a little nubby tail, and an energy level that tops out around a 7 on most days with occasional zoomies thrown in for good measure. Josie is a six-year-old hound mix, about 35 pounds, and she's been around the block once already. She was adopted for a couple of months but got returned because her energy wasn't a match for that family. That happens. It just means she needs the right fit, not the first fit.

She went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups immersive training program and came out knowing sit, stay, and more. She walks on a leash, enjoys a good play session, and then fully expects to claim her spot on the couch next to you afterward. Active during the day, cuddly in the evenings. That's her whole vibe.

She does best as an only dog and is not a match for cats. She hasn't been around younger kids yet, but her foster thinks kids 10 and up would be a good fit since she plays hard and can get a little mouthy during play. Nothing aggressive, just enthusiastic. She's currently in a foster home and doing well.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw on Chastain Road. You can visit their website or call to set up a time to meet Josie.

blurb:
Three months old, four and a half pounds, and completely ready to take over your couch. Dionne is one of Mostly Mutts' Clueless-themed kittens — she and her sister were pulled from animal control, spent time in a foster home, and have now landed back at the shelter where the volunteers have been happily spoiling them while they wait for the right families.

She's curious, playful, and genuinely affectionate. Her days run on a pretty reliable loop: play hard, recharge with a nap, play again. She loves kitten toys and loves cuddle time just as much. She gets along great with her sister, so if you've already got a cat at home who might enjoy a small, energetic new friend, that could be a great setup. Kids are welcome as long as they're gentle with her. Dogs are still an unknown.

She's microchipped and has started her kitten vaccinations — you'll need to finish those as she grows. She's not spayed yet because she's still a little small, but Mostly Mutts requires it and will cover the cost through one of their approved North Metro Atlanta vets. That does mean they're keeping adoptions local.

Her adoption fee is $175. You can find her full profile at mostlymutts.org or visit their Kennesaw location to meet her in person.

blurb:
Two pounds of Seinfeld-themed trouble, and he's looking for a home. Jerry is about two and a half months old, came into Mostly Mutts after being rescued from animal control, and has been living his best kitten life in a foster home ever since. He's ready for his next chapter.

He spends his days doing exactly what you'd expect — chasing toys, pouncing on things, wrestling with his siblings, and then completely crashing and demanding to be in someone's lap. High energy when he's on, completely cuddly when he's done. The volunteers describe him as sweet and playful, and his foster home has kids as young as 11 who he gets along with just fine. He's also done well with the dogs in his foster home, so if you have a cat-friendly dog, there's a real shot they figure it out together.

He'll need to be neutered once he hits the right size, and Mostly Mutts covers that cost through one of their approved vets in the North Metro Atlanta area, so they're keeping adoptions local.

If you've been on the fence about adding a kitten, Jerry is a pretty solid reason to get off it. Check out his profile at mostlymutts.org or stop by their Kennesaw location to meet him.

blurb:
This guy has been through more than most cats will ever see, and he's still sweet as ever. Peeta is a five-and-a-half-year-old Domestic Shorthair/Siamese mix who was originally adopted from Mostly Mutts as a kitten — one of their Hunger Games-themed litters. Life happened, he came back. Got adopted again, then accidentally swallowed a string that wrapped around his tongue and worked its way into his GI tract. He needed emergency surgery. He came through it. And now he's ready to try again.

Once he got settled in his foster home, he opened all the way up. He's the kind of cat who winds up underfoot looking for attention, leans into pets, and just wants to be near his person. Not aloof. Not complicated. Just genuinely affectionate and looking for somewhere to land for good.

He's lived with other cats before and did well, so a home with another mellow cat could work nicely. Kids are fine as long as they're gentle with him. Dogs are an unknown, so a meet and greet would be the move there. He's litter trained and fully recovered from surgery.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can browse his profile online and reach out through their website to get the adoption process started.

He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, found a foster family who loves him, and his foster says he lights up every room he walks into. That's not marketing language. blurb:
Meeko is 12 years old, 33 pounds, and his foster family calls him a treasure. Not a good dog. A treasure. He also has a security blanket, which is an old towel he's apparently very attached to, and honestly that detail alone should tell you everything you need to know about this guy.

He's a Jack Russell-Greyhound mix with a spunky, playful side that his age has not slowed down one bit. He knows sit, down, stay, come, and something called "last call" which is apparently a cue for a final potty break before bed. His foster says he sometimes seems to read her mind. He cuddles, he plays with toys, he walks nicely on a leash, and he doesn't jump on people. At 12, he has figured out how to be a really good dog.

He'd do best as your only dog. He's gotten used to other dogs in foster situations with slow introductions, but he'd genuinely prefer not to share. Mostly Mutts also recommends calm kids 15 and up for him.

If you have a quieter home and want a companion who's going to curl up next to you, learn your schedule, and bring his little towel with him, Meeko is worth a visit. He's at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw.

• The security blanket detail is an instant emotional hook that makes Meeko unforgettable in a newsletter format
